claims.text_en: Sathon is one of Bangkok's 50 khets, 9.326 km2 south of the CBD, with three khwaeng: Thung Wat Don (3.195 km2, 34,618 people), Yan Nawa (2.090, 18,132) and Thung Maha Mek (4.041, 18,556) - 71,306 registered residents in Dec 2023. Boundaries (Thai Wikipedia): north - Bang Rak/Pathum Wan along Khlong Sathon and the south side of Rama IV; east - Khlong Toei/Yan Nawa along the Mae Nam railway line, Soi Chuea Phloeng 4 and Yen Akat road; south - Yan Nawa/Bang Kho Laem along Nang Linchi, Chan Kao, Khlong Chong Nonsi, Chan and Sathupradit roads to Khlong Khuay; west - the river midline (Khlong San across). The khet was created 9 November 1989 from Yan Nawa (branch office from 9 March 1989); the spelling สาธร was officially corrected in April 1999.

claims.text_en: The office-district identity sits on a corridor the app polygon excludes: English Wikipedia states Sathon Road 'marks the northern boundary of the district', with the southern lanes in Sathon and the northern lanes across Sathon canal in Bang Rak - and PIP confirms the app polygon hugs the road's south side, putting the BTS Surasak, Chong Nonsi and Saint Louis station nodes (all standing in the road median) OUTSIDE the sathon polygon, along with office towers on the north side, while the south sidewalk is IN. The Empire Tower, AIA Sathorn Tower, At Sathorn Square, Robot Building and the 12+ embassies of Thai Wikipedia's list are the khet's daytime economy but mostly lie on or beyond the excluded strip; Saint Louis Hospital, MR Kukrit's House, Suan Phlu market and Wat Yannawa are PIP-IN.

claims.text_en: Why transport 7 and not 9: the BTS Silom Line (Surasak, Chong Nonsi, Saint Louis, with Saphan Taksin at the north-west corner) and MRT Lumphini serve the khet's north and north-east edges only - and all three mid-corridor BTS nodes fall outside the app polygon, which begins at the south side of Sathorn Rd. The interior - Yen Akat, Chan, Nang Linchi, Thung Wat Don's sois - sits roughly a kilometre or more from any rail gate. The BRT's Chong Nonsi-Ratchaphruek corridor does cross the khet on Narathiwas Road (BRT Sathon stop PIP-IN), and the Chao Phraya express boat calls at Tha Sathorn; but the modal mix is edge-loaded, which is the honest mechanism for a 7.

claims.text_en: The Chong Nonsi canal park is the khet's flagship public project and its messiest: a 4.5 km linear park along Khlong Chong Nonsi by LANDPROCESS (Kotchakorn Voraakhom, modelled in part on Seoul's Cheonggyecheon), Thailand's first canal-park of its kind, with nature-based water treatment whose water-quality gains The Nation (11 Jul 2026) reports 'slower than anticipated'; search-aggregated BMA reporting has Phase 3 (Narathiwas Soi 7 to Chan Rd, ~1.6 km, ~472M THB announced Aug 2024) under construction through 2025 with completion targeted end-2025 by Deputy Governor Wisanu, and users complaining of black, odorous canal water in dry periods when the level is drawn down. The mapped park segment (PIP-IN) is the built proof of concept.

claims.text_en: Rental market (HipFlat, October 2026): 8,231 listings - by far the deepest stock of the four khets - with average asking USD 475 for studios, USD 889 for 1-bedrooms and USD 1,730 for 2-bedrooms (USD 19/sqm), from a 23,000-THB Klass Silom 1-bed to 490,000-THB ONE89 2-beds; visible clusters sit on the Silom/Saladaeng edge, central Sathorn Rd and the Charoen Krung riverfront (The River), not in the Yen Akat/Chan interior. Prices drifting down (-5.8% vs Jan 2026). The app's 25,000/55,000 blend sits below the portal's 1-bed mean - consistent with the inland mid-market half of the khet; rent 5 (priciest of the four) is defensible.

question_answers.notes: Khet Sathon, 9.326 km2, three khwaeng (Thung Wat Don, Yan Nawa, Thung Maha Mek), bounded by Khlong Sathon + Rama IV south side (N), the Mae Nam railway/Yen Akat (E), Nang Linchi/Chan/Khlong Chong Nonsi/Sathupradit (S), river midline (W); created 9 Nov 1989 from Yan Nawa. In-polygon anchors: Saint Louis Hospital, MR Kukrit's House, Suan Phlu market, Wat Yannawa, 80 Phansa park, Taksin bridge park, canal-park segments, Wat Don cemetery, BRT Sathon stop. Out: the three BTS nodes (Surasak/Chong Nonsi/Saint Louis, in the road median), Sathorn Unique tower, Suan Pa Chaloem Phra Kiat tip, MRT Lumphini.

CBD-south office khet with a residential interior: weekday Sathorn-corridor suits and embassy traffic, canal-park and royal-park weekends, quiet Yen Akat/Chan sois with heritage houses inland; the mall-and-BTS strip belongs to the excluded boundary. Subarea claims marked partial.

Transport 7 = edge-loaded rail (three BTS nodes on the excluded corridor, MRT Lumphini just off the NE corner) plus the BRT Narathiwas corridor and Tha Sathorn boat - the interior is a km+ from any rail gate. DE 9 / food 9 = office-crowd market/cafe density (1,098 food POIs) + Suan Phlu/Wat Yannawa anchors. Green 9 = named-park access (80 Phansa 3.02 ha, canal park, Taksin bridge park) rather than in-khet acreage. Rent 5 = deepest stock (8,231 listings) and highest prices of the four khets.

Three: (1) green 9 cannot be reproduced from mapped in-khet green (~5-6 ha PIP-IN vs app 25.0 ha) - the score rides on named-park access, not acreage; (2) transport 7 is internally consistent only because the polygon excludes the BTS corridor the khet is famous for; (3) the canal park's water quality remains visibly poor ('slower than anticipated', odor complaints), tempering the green story.

Office mornings and lunch pulses on the corridor; embassy/school rhythms inland; the canal park and royal park (05:00-21:00) carry morning runners and evening aerobics; weekends move to parks and the riverside; nightlife concentrates on the north corridor around Chong Nonsi.

Flat interior grid; the canal-park walkways and the royal-park loop give genuine walking infrastructure; Sathorn Rd itself is a hostile, congested crossing; no walking durations were derived from catchment radius in this bundle.

Daily needs: Suan Phlu and neighbourhood wet markets, office-tower retail, Saint Louis Hospital + schools for the family layer, 12+ embassies for paperwork; leisure: 80 Phansa park, canal park, Wat Yannawa riverside, MR Kukrit's House museum.

App 25,000/55,000 sits below HipFlat's portal means (1-bed USD 889 ~ 30k THB; 2-bed USD 1,730 ~ 59-60k) because the portal set skews Silom-edge and riverfront; the inland mid-market band (Nang Linchi/Yen Akat) is what pulls the blend down. Rent 5 = priciest of the four khets; prices gently falling (-5.8% vs Jan 2026).

Green: named parks are real and inside (80 Phansa renovated 2025-26, canal-park segments, Taksin bridge park, cemetery green) but the 25.0-ha app figure needs a counting rule; the 2.63-ha forest park at the west tip is polygon-OUT. Quiet: genuine in the interior sois; the corridor and Narathiwas BRT carry the noise. The excluded Sathorn corridor means 'Sathon address' and 'polygon interior' diverge for offices and nightlife.

Strong fit: office-district professionals who want walk-to-work plus real parks (renovated royal park, canal park) and can pay CBD-south rents. Weak fit: budget renters (priciest of the four) and anyone whose daily life depends on being AT a BTS gate - the gates are on the excluded corridor, a km+ from the interior.

80 Phansa royal park renovation (2025-2026); canal-park Phase 3 built out along Chan Road through 2025 (end-2025 target, unconfirmed); Blue & Green Network program active into 2026; rents drifting down; no rail changes inside the khet.

Unresolved: the 25.0-ha park counting rule (OSM ~5-6 ha in-polygon); whether Phase 3 of the canal park actually completed end-2025 (target only); BRT service details (no ridership/fare data body-read); khet membership of individual corridor towers; rent data single-family (PropertyScout 404). Safety 7 untested by any located statistic.

preview.text_en: The CBD's south annex: embassy rows, office towers and a renovated royal park along a canal being turned into Bangkok's first linear water-garden - at the batch's highest rents, with the BTS gates sitting on the boundary line the map excludes.

guide_lead.text_en: Sathon wraps three khwaeng of residential sois around the Sathorn office corridor, with the deepest rental stock of the batch (8,231 listings), 12+ embassies, Saint Louis Hospital, and the batch's best named-park access - the 80 Phansa royal park reopened in 2025-2026 with expanded green, and the 4.5 km Chong Nonsi canal park keeps extending even as its water quality lags. The honest asterisks: the BTS stations that give the district its name sit in the road median the app polygon excludes (transport 7, not 9), the 25-ha green figure needs a counting rule, and rents - though slipping - remain the priciest of the four researched khets.

strengths.text_en: Parks you can actually use: the renovated 80 Phansa royal park (05:00-21:00, lit loop, playground, stage) plus the canal-park walkway segments and Taksin bridge park - the batch's strongest named-green access.
Office-district completeness: Saint Louis Hospital and schools, 1,098 food POIs, wet markets inland, and a BRT corridor threading Narathiwas - daily life rarely requires leaving the khet.

tradeoffs.text_en: The transit paradox: three BTS stations carry the district's name but stand in the median the polygon excludes, leaving interior sois (Yen Akat, Chan, Nang Linchi) a kilometre-plus from any rail gate - hence transport 7.
Priciest of the batch: portal 1-bed averages ~USD 889 (~30k THB) with the blend at 25,000/55,000, and the canal park's water is still visibly poor despite the 2024-2026 build-out.

conditional_fit.text_en: Choose it if you work in the CBD and want a walkable green routine (royal park loop, canal walkways) and full services at 25-30k for a 1-bed - and don't mind the BTS being a boundary feature rather than a door-step one.
Skip it if rent is the constraint (cheapest 1-beds here cost what Thon Buri charges for two) or if you need rail at the door in the interior sois.
